# Instructions

For this final milestone, apply what you have learned about data visualization to create "publication ready" artifacts of your analysis. You'll use what you've learned to create a table and a plot that you could publish as part of a journal article or company report.

Use at least three related graphs to investigate a variable (or variables) of interest in this data. Your approach should be iterative (graph 2 builds on graph 1) and move you toward better understanding a question of your choosing.

Alternatively, return to a previous milestone and produce a publication-quality table or graph using the skills you have learned this week. Some ideas:

1. Choose a data visualization from earlier in this course and further customize your graph using themes, annotations, labels and/or aesthetics with ggplot2

2. Create a table, or choose a table you created earlier in this course, and use gt to build the table into an effective standalone figure, including colored cells and a footnote

To learn more about the variables contained in the data set, refer to the data dictionary: https://rstudio.github.io/academy-tidyverse-stock-portfolios/assets/indexes_dictionary.html

# Milestone

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# loading packages
library(tidyverse)
```

## Data visualization

To help you get started, the code below builds several portfolios that allocate x% of their funds to an S&P 500 index and (100 - x)% of their funds to a 10 year treasury bill. You may wish to use this as the basis for a publication-ready table (with the gt package) and a polished plot (with ggplot2), or start fresh with a question of your own.

```{r}
#| label: portfolios
#| eval: false
indexes <- read_csv("data/indexes.csv")

portfolios <-
  indexes |>
  filter(symbol %in% c("^GSPC", "^TNX")) |>
  group_by(symbol) |>
  mutate(
    return = 1 + ((adjusted - lag(adjusted)) / lag(adjusted)),
    return = if_else(is.na(return), 1, return),
    symbol = case_when(
      symbol == "^GSPC" ~ "GSPC",
      symbol == "^TNX"  ~ "TNX"
    )
  ) |>
  select(date, symbol, return) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = symbol, values_from = return) |>
  mutate(
    sp500_75 = .75 * GSPC + .25 * TNX,
    sp500_50 = .50 * GSPC + .50 * TNX,
    sp500_25 = .25 * GSPC + .75 * TNX
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "symbol", values_to = "return")

portfolios
```
